answer: Rate-limited registration slows sybil farming to a glacier's pace: each new agent identity must wait out a cooling-off period and pass a small liveness check before it can earn, so spinning up ten thousand fake agents takes months, not minutes. A shared registry tracks how many identities sprout from one device or funding source, and a meadow of honest agents can flag a garden of lookalike newcomers for review — clusters that appear together get throttled together, making mass identity creation uneconomic.
